 Live .  8,268 viewing 8268 viewing Live page Updated 1 minute ago 'Wow, I'm lost for words' - Hamilton takes first pole for Ferrari in Mexico
 Live Reporting (active) 
 Leaderboard 
 Summary
 Hamilton takes pole position for Mexico City Grand Prix - his first for Ferrari
 'I love what I do, that love is not gone' - Hamilton reaction here 
 Mercedes driver Russell second and Leclerc in third - report here 
 Antonelli, who starts fourth, will become world champion with ninth place in Sunday's race
 How to follow weekend action on BBC | latest F1 Q&A 
 Close form Send us your F1 views
 Get involved Live Reporting
 Lorraine McKenna
 'Hit rate too low at the moment' - Russell published at 22:37 GMT 22:37 GMT 
 Image source, Getty Images Mercedes' George Russell, who will start on the front row in P2: "It's been a tricky few races for me, still struggling to get on top of this car to be honest, because it's been a very difficult weekend up until one lap in Q3. And to find half a second to almost get pole from Lewis [Hamilton], obviously it was really close in the end. 
 "I always know it's in there, the performance is in there, but the hit rate is too low at the moment. So that's sort of the frustration I have. 
 "But of course, happy with this front row." 
 3 1 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Where there is a will there is a way' published at 22:33 GMT 22:33 GMT 
 Image source, Getty Images Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton, who will start tomorrow's race on pole position: "Wow. That feels great, that feels good. I am so happy. I am lost for words.
 "It has been a really tough, challenging weekend. We did a good job with the setup over the weekend but it is so close between us all.
 "To have pole here, wow, I don't know if I've got one here before? It is my first pole with Ferrari.
 "When there is a will there is a way. It is all in the mind for all of us. You might feel aches and pains but luckily I don't. I love what I do, that love is not gone. I wake up every day thinking about it and I dream about it. I have this amazing support around the world. I hope I can deliver for them tomorrow."

 Post published at 22:31 GMT 22:31 GMT 
 Marc Priestley 
Former F1 mechanic on Radio 5 Live in Mexico City 
 Hamilton and Russell are the two who can stop Antonelli becoming champion on Sunday and they are the two who start on the front row.
 64 5 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Hamilton takes maiden Ferrari pole published at 22:27 GMT 22:27 GMT 
 Image source, Getty Images With more than 100 career pole positions to his name, it's amazing to think this is Lewis Hamilton's maiden pole for Italian team Ferrari. The seven-time world champion was almost lost for words on the radio, and now he'll have the chance to add to his Scuderia win tally tomorrow. 
 If Hamilton does triumph at the Mexico City Grand Prix, he will need title leader Kimi Antonelli to finish outside the points to roll the championship fight over to Brazil next weekend.

 Chequered flag published at 22:10 GMT 22:10 GMT 
 Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton will start on pole position for the Mexico City Grand Prix! 
 What a lap by the seven-time world champion. That's Hamilton's first pole since he was a Mercedes driver at the Hungarian Grand Prix in 2023! 
 His former team-mate George Russell will start alongside him on the front row - the two drivers who need to win the race tomorrow to keep their title hopes alive.

 Antonelli goes P5 published at 22:10 GMT 22:10 GMT 
 Kimi Antonelli doesn't need to be on pole on Sunday, and it looks like fifth will have to do for the champion in waiting. 
 Max Verstappen has locked up on his challenge for pole and has to settle for fourth on the grid. 
 So that means...

 Hamilton beats Russell's time published at 22:09 GMT 22:09 GMT 
 But it doesn't last long, as the Ferrari of Lewis Hamilton goes 0.009 seconds quicker than George Russell to snatch provisional pole away from the Mercedes man. 
 Charles Leclerc's latest lap can only put him third on the board.

 Verstappen beats Norris' time published at 22:03 GMT 22:03 GMT 
 The front row gets demoted to the second for Lando Norris, as Max Verstappen puts down a lap time of 1:16.692 to slip into P2 on these opening runs in Q3. 
 Verstappen had a decent final sector, and is 0.045 seconds off Charles Leclerc marker. But the Dutchman has that one-place grid penalty for his contact with Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson yesterday. 
 100 86 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Norris on the front row published at 22:01 GMT 22:01 GMT 
 Lando Norris puts his McLaren on the front row, but the world champion is is 0.177 seconds behind provisional polesitter Charles Leclerc. 
 118 47 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Leclerc goes quickest published at 22:00 GMT 22:00 GMT 
 Lewis Hamilton just makes a little mistake in the middle sector which stops him going quickest on his first push lap. The other Ferrari of Charles Leclerc gets round fine, and goes top of the timesheets with a 1:16.647. 
 George Russell's attempt is good enough for the second row in P3, while Kimi Antonelli can only manage fourth with his opening time. 
 101 38 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 21:57 GMT 21:57 GMT 
 So, who made it through to Q3? The big dogs are all there, minus one of the McLarens, and are joined by the two Racing Bulls of Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad, plus the Alpine of Pierre Gasly.
